meta.title: Gatekeeper
meta.description: Three tools, split by what a call does to the project rather than by which file it emits. py-audit reads: which lockfile manages the dependencies (and it refuses to push uv into a Poetry/PDM/Pipenv project), the declared Python version and where it came from, which of ruff/mypy/ty/pytest/pre-commit are configured, what 13 static rules say about the workflows already there, which of the nine generated artefacts are missing, whether the git pre-commit hook points at prek, the order the thirteen quality gates run in (eight mandatory, five opt-in), and the values the pipeline resolves with their source; plus sixteen bundled skill documents by topic. py-scaffold writes: a dry-run preview of the nine files this plugin generates (the pyproject tables, prek hooks, Dependabot, a thirteen-stage Python/uv GitHub Actions workflow split into four jobs, the same gates as a standard-library scripts/ci.py, the version manifest, and the manifest, secret-scan and container-report scripts), written only on request to those nine fixed paths, backup first. py-run executes those same gates locally in pipeline order (--profile commit for the pre-commit subset, --from to resume at a stage), optionally including the integration, dependency-audit and container stages, dry-run by default. The panel shows the thirteen-stage matrix with each stage's CI job and needs, the project facts (including the commit hook and the six reported-only image checks), the nine generated artefacts, and the resolved values with their source; a chip above the composer opens one foldable group per tool — three in all — holding sixteen modes, putting the picked mode's real skill token into the draft.
